Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus budget of a GLM-AED lake

Source: R/glm_budget.R
diag_glm_budget.Rd

Combines the process and interface fluxes from the GLM-AED diagnostic output (calc_glm_fluxes()) with the inflow, outflow and in-lake inventory from the mass balance (diag_glm_mass_balance()) to give, for each element, where it comes from, where it goes, and how much of the change in the inventory those terms explain.

Usage

diag_glm_budget(
  aeme,
  element = c("N", "P", "C"),
  period = c("all", "year", "month"),
  path = NULL,
  include_spin_up = TRUE,
  settling = c("hypsograph", "interface")
)

Arguments

aeme

Aeme object that has been run with glm_aed. Not needed if file is given.

element

character; any of "C", "N" and "P".

period

character; summary resolution, "all" (default, the whole run), "year" or "month".

path

character; root directory used with aeme.

include_spin_up

logical; keep the spin-up period? If FALSE, days before the simulation start are dropped.

settling

character; "hypsograph" (default) or "interface", see calc_glm_fluxes().

Value

a list with

  • fluxes: one row per element, period and process between two compartments (from, to), with the mean rate mmol_d, the equivalent kg_yr (kg of the element per year) and the areal mmol_m2_d (per m2 of mean lake surface).

  • pools: the mean inventory of each compartment (mmol and kg), from the AED totals of the model configuration.

  • closure: per element and period, the terms inflow, outflow, sediment, atmosphere, explained, d_storage and residual, in the same three units. Positive means a gain for the lake.

  • compartments: the same closure for each compartment (inorganic, phyto, dom, pom): its d_storage and the inflow, outflow, flux_in and flux_out of every diagnostic flux entering or leaving it, including from other compartments, and the residual they do not explain. A compartment with a large residual has a process or exchange that is mis-reported or missing: this is where to look when a concentration drifts.

  • daily: daily net boundary flux and mass balance terms behind closure, in mmol/d.

Details

The lake is treated as one pool made of the compartments inorganic, phyto, dom and pom (for carbon, inorganic is DIC and is outside the pool, as it is not part of TOC). A flux that crosses the boundary of that pool adds to or removes from the inventory. Anything between two compartments inside the pool (uptake, mortality, mineralisation, nitrification, ...) is internal and cancels. The closure is

residual = d(inventory) - (inflow - outflow + sediment + atmosphere)

where sediment is the net exchange across the sediment-water interface (dissolved release minus settling) and atmosphere is deposition and gas exchange, including N2 fixation and denitrification for nitrogen. A residual near zero means the diagnostics account for the budget. A persistent residual points to a source or sink the diagnostics do not report, for example a module that is not writing its *_swi terms, or a mismatch between how a pool is settled and how it is resuspended.

The fluxes are the instantaneous rates AED writes at each save time. On the example lake a residual of 3 to 13% of the gross primary production remained with settling, hydrolysis, resuspension and outflow switched off, with hourly instead of daily output, with a ten times shorter time step and with thinner layers, and it disappeared when growth was switched off. It therefore follows the production terms (PHY_upt_*) rather than the other pathways, and is not a sampling or resolution effect. Compare the residual with the largest flux, not with the change in storage, which can be close to zero.

The inflow, outflow and inventory need the totals in the mass balance: TN, TP and TOC are all in the default balance_vars (see set_glm_balance_groups() and add_glm_balance_vars()). Without them closure is NULL for that element but the fluxes and pools are still returned.

See also

plot_glm_budget() for a box-and-arrow figure of the result.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bud <- diag_glm_budget(aeme, element = c("N", "P"))
bud$closure
plot_glm_budget(bud)
} # }
